title: refactor(ci): consolidate Node.js workflows, upgrade to Node 20, and standardize lint/test matrices
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: our repo has accumulated multiple Node.js CI workflows across services and SDKs (node16/node18-specific files, duplicated setup logic, and inconsistent test matrices). This PR consolidates workflows into a small set of reusable templates, upgrades the primary CI to Node 20, and standardizes lint/test matrices to reduce flakiness and speed up runs.

What this PR does (summary):
- Consolidate multiple .github/workflows/*ci-*.yml into two canonical templates: workflows/ci.yml (unit/lint) and workflows/integration.yml.
- Upgrade the default Node runtime to Node 20 across workflows and helper scripts (uses actions/setup-node@v4).
- Standardize test matrices: node: [20], os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest] for SDKs where coverage matters; keep node 18 only for legacy-compat tests via a nightly matrix in a single workflow.
- Move shared shell logic to .github/ci-scripts/setup-node.sh and reference via workflow uses to reduce duplication.
- Improve caching for node_modules and pnpm store by switching to actions/cache with key scoped to package-lock/pnpm-lock and node-version.
- Remove legacy node16 workflows and retirement notice in README CI section.
- Update release automation integration (scripts/release.js) to be compatible with Node 20 and the consolidated workflows; run a dry-run of the release job in CI.

Checklist:
- [x] Consolidated workflow files and removed duplicates
- [x] Upgraded Node runtime references to 20 where applicable
- [x] Ensured actions/setup-node uses v4 and pnpm/npm caching updated
- [x] Updated release script and verified dry-run in CI
- [x] Ran smoke tests across redwood, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript examples

Testing and validation:
- Ran full CI across the monorepo on a feature branch: node-lint, unit-tests, integration-tests, release-dry-run. All checks passed after a single rerun for a flaky browser test in integration.
- Verified that publish paths and release tags are unchanged by the refactor via the dry-run in the release job.
- Performed local end-to-end tests of the SDK build matrix on macos/latest and ubuntu.

Migration notes for integrators:
- Any repo-level custom workflows that previously referenced removed files should point to .github/workflows/ci.yml using the documented inputs in .github/workflows/README (added).
- If consumers relied on node 16 behavior, they should pin to the legacy-nightly workflow; a deprecation note is in the top-level README with links to a migration guide.

Rollout: staged merge — started with redwood repo, then applied same templates to SDK repos (redwood-sdk-node, redwood-sdk-python wrappers) via follow-up PRs. No runtime behavior changes expected for production code; this is strictly CI/build infra and release tooling.

review_thread: Ethan Blake (reviewer) — 2025-11-13: Nice consolidation. A couple questions: can we keep one job with matrix including node 18 for backward compatibility instead of a separate nightly? Also requested add a short migration note in README.

Maya Thompson (author) — 2025-11-13: Reply: I tried to keep the main CI fast by moving node 18 to a nightly matrix. That keeps our primary runs quick while preserving compatibility checks. Added README migration notes as requested.

Priya Menon (reviewer) — 2025-11-15: Please ensure setup-node v4 is pinned in the action input and that cache keys include node-version for cross-version cache safety. Also flagged a flaky browser test in integration that needs special attention.

Maya Thompson (author) — 2025-11-16: Addressed: pinned setup-node@v4, updated cache keys to include node-version and lockfile hash. I also adjusted the integration test retry to be explicit for the flaky test (added --retries=2 in the job).
Noah Kim (approver) — 2025-11-18: LGTM after the updates. Approving for merge. CI looked stable on the latest run.

release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows and standardized Node runtime to Node 20.
Improved caching and reduced CI duplication which should decrease average run time.
Legacy Node 16 workflows removed; Node 18 compatibility runs moved to a nightly matrix.
Release automation updated for Node 20 (no change to published artifacts).
